newsitem.title: USA: "Fatal Vision" killer files for retrial in N.C..
newsitem.headline: "Fatal Vision" killer files for retrial in N.C..

text.p: Attorneys for Jeffrey MacDonald, a U.S. Army doctor accused of killing his pregnant wife and two young daughters, have asked for a new trial based on recent allegations the FBI crime lab mishandled evidence.

The Feb. 17, 1970, killing at Fort Bragg was the subject of newspaper stories, movies and books, the best known of which was "Fatal Vision" by Joe McGinniss, and the case went all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court. MacDonald, 53, who is serving three life sentences in a federal prison in Sheridan, Oregon, has staunchly maintained his innocence.

"I think there still is unease about this case," he said in an interview in Wednesday's Charlotte Observer. "It is one of those events when the country was in so much turmoil that it is imprinted on people's brains."

MacDonald contends four "drug-crazed hippies" repeatedly stabbed him on the night of the killings, leaving him unconscious while they bludgeoned his family with a club. His defence had tried and failed to reopen the case in 1990.

In the 1,500 pages of documents filed in U.S. District Court in Raleigh on Tuesday, his defence team said the judge who rejected the appeal for a new trial in 1990 had relied on testimony from Michael Malone, an FBI fiber specialist who was criticised in a U.S. Justice Department report last week.
The report said the FBI's crime laboratories had provided flawed evidence in several major cases including the Oklahoma City and World Trade Centre bombings.

After the report, FBI officials said several hundred cases were being reviewed for exculpatory evidence that would help defendants win new trials or overturn their convictions but expressed confidence the government would prevail in most.
